summary: The change is correct and minimal. In createHand the n===2 branch sets sb=button and bb=dealOrder[0]. The existing first-actor rule (clockwiseAfter(seats, bb)[0]) then picks the button preflop. endRound's open[0] (clockwise from the button) picks the non-button seat postflop. Deal order (K4) and splitPot's odd-chip order are unchanged and correct for heads-up (D-2, D-3). The 3..10-seat path does not change by construction. I re-ran the 6-max baseline and got Ended by fold 5470, showdown 4530, Player actions 88831, capped 244, Largest pot $70, the same replay codes and 0 violations, which matches spec section 3. The --size 2 run gives 10000 hands and 0 violations in about 0.3 s. Interplay with TASK-1.9: I ran ad-hoc heads-up checks (short button calling all-in, short BB calling all-in, BB folding to a raise, button folding to a raise with button=2). All ran out to showdown or folded out with the right uncalled returns, non-button-first split ordering, and checkStep/checkState reporting []. The tests would catch a regression: reverting the blind fix breaks the AC#1 exact action records, AC#2 toAct and legalActions, AC#4 hand-walk and AC#5 Preflop line. SPEC-08 pins the award, returned and stacks. Size: 346 lines against a 280 budget, of which about 19 are src. The rest are tests the spec requires (two new acceptance files with copied helpers, as section 3 says), so the overrun is justified. About 10 lines in the SPEC-09 unit test are redundant (MINOR). No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
